# Operability Checklist: ISK-0010 — System-Operator Bootstrap & Security Baseline

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for audit records, diagnostics, the developer topology, and the operator runbook are complete, unambiguous, and measurable
**Created**: 2026-11-21
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Audit records

- [x] CHK001 - Is each audit record's field set specified, with the values each enumerated field may take? [Completeness, Spec §FR-027, Contract §Audit records 2 and 4]
- [x] CHK002 - Is every field's source defined for records written by the `bootstrap` command, which has no request? [Gap, Contract §Audit records 2, Data model §OperatorRequestContext]
- [x] CHK003 - Is the set of events that write a record, and the set that never does, stated without overlap? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028, Contract §Audit records 4 and 5]
- [x] CHK004 - Is "a record exists if and only if its change committed" stated, and is the append-only rule enforced by the database? [Measurability, Spec §FR-026, §FR-029, Persistence §Isolation 11]
- [x] CHK005 - Are audit retention and tamper-evident ordering explicitly deferred, with their owning spec? [Traceability, Spec §AV-6, Contract §Audit records 6]

## Diagnostics

- [x] CHK006 - Are the event IDs, names, levels, and templates fixed, with each placeholder's allowed values? [Clarity, Spec §FR-037, Contract §Diagnostics]
- [x] CHK007 - Are metric names, kinds, and label values bounded so no label can carry a request path, principal, or address? [Clarity, Spec §FR-038, Contract §Diagnostics 3]
- [x] CHK008 - Is a flood-safe rule stated for the limit event, so a flood cannot flood the log? [Edge Case, Contract §Diagnostics 2]
- [x] CHK009 - Is the leak canary's search scope stated measurably (which outputs, which values)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004, Contract §Test fixture 3]

## Developer topology

- [x] CHK010 - Is the control plane's published port specified (loopback only, default, override) with nothing else newly published? [Completeness, Spec §FR-034, Local environment §Ports]
- [x] CHK011 - Is the bootstrap script's interface, delivery of the token, and exit codes specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-035, Local environment §Scripts, §Exit codes]
- [x] CHK012 - Are the new smoke assertions specified exactly, including how a well-formed token is generated without a fixed value? [Clarity, Spec §FR-036, Local environment §Smoke assertions 8 to 10]
- [x] CHK013 - Is it stated that the three readiness answers stay byte for byte unchanged, and that a change to the expected smoke state is a revision? [Consistency, Spec §FR-036, Local environment §Changing this contract]
- [x] CHK014 - Is each plane's document layout for transport stated (base valid outside `development`, overlay `none`)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-035, Local environment §Documents 2 and 3]

## Runbook and upgrade

- [x] CHK015 - Does the runbook requirement name every operator task it covers: issue, redeem, enrollment, recovery, TLS, publishing, audit, diagnostics, rollback, and known limits? [Completeness, Spec §FR-041, Plan §Constitution Check VIII]
- [x] CHK016 - Is the upgrade effect of the new transport default on an existing manifest stated, with the operator's action? [Coverage, Plan §Risks]
- [x] CHK017 - Is the pre-ISK-0021 state (every admin route `503`, every command exit 5) stated where an operator will read it? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, Contract §Known limits]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Review 2026-11-21, first pass: CHK002 failed, because a `bootstrap` command run has no request to take a correlation ID from. The contract's Audit records rule 2 now says the run generates one correlation ID and uses the revision of the documents it validated. Re-reviewed and passed.
